commits.message:
feat(email-parsing): push published job requirements to Jobfynder Core

The last step of the pipeline: email -> parsed -> landed in Hermes's own
database -> claim-and-verify confirmed (or manually approved) ->
published in Hermes -> only then -> pushed to Core's job board. Nothing
before "published" ever reaches Core, matching the "Hermes proposes,
Core executes" boundary (docs/hermes-architecture-frozen-v1.md section
2). Wired into the one existing choke point both the claim flow and
manual review already go through: publish_draft_object().

New: app/integrations/core_job_push.py, calling Core's existing internal
endpoint POST /api/hermes/job/create (shared-secret bearer auth, not a
user login -- HermesAuthGuard in jobFynder-BE-nestJS). That endpoint
always creates the job as Core's own DRAFT status too -- this push does
not make anything live on the job board; Core's separate publish step
still gates that. Two independent "nothing goes live automatically"
guarantees, not one.

Every pushed job is attributed to a fixed system account on Core
(HERMES_SOURCING_USER_ID) -- the real external recruiter is captured via
externalSource/recruiterInfo instead. Field mapping is deliberately
best-effort where it has to be: Hermes extracts free-text (a raw
location string, a raw rate string), Core expects some fields pre-
classified against its own taxonomy tables with case-insensitive exact
matching. A recruiter's claim corrections (draft.metadata.claimed_fields)
are preferred over the raw parse for every field they could differ on.
Employment type is the one hard requirement Core enforces -- if Hermes
never determined one, the push fails loudly with that exact reason
rather than inventing "Contract" out of thin air (verified: a missing
employment_type is simply omitted from the payload, not guessed).

Every attempt is recorded in core_pushes (success or failure) and on the
draft's own metadata -- never raises, so a Core outage or a bad token
can never turn a successful Hermes-side publish into a failed one.

Retrieved the existing HERMES_SERVICE_TOKEN from Core's own .env (it
already existed there, provisioned for this exact guard) and copied it
into Hermes's .env along with CORE_API_BASE_URL -- piped directly
between the two servers' shells so the value was never displayed in any
terminal output or file this session wrote.

Confirmed Core's production server (72.62.194.11) is running main, not
features -- the job-creation upgrade from the earlier commit on that
repo (feat(hermes): accept full parsed job payload on POST
/hermes/job/create) is not live there yet. Per explicit decision, this
commit stays Hermes-side only: it does not deploy Core's features
branch. Calling the currently-live (old, minimal) endpoint will fail
with "platform_user_id required" until that happens -- confirmed
deliberately as the correct, safe behavior for now, not a bug: the
failure is recorded, not silently swallowed, and nothing here assumes
Core has already caught up.

Verified: 15 new tests (rate/location text parsing across several real-
world formats, full payload mapping including claim-correction override
and the missing-employment-type-must-not-be-guessed guarantee, HTTP
success/failure/not-configured paths with urlopen mocked, and confirming
publish_draft_object() itself still succeeds when the Core push fails).
Full existing 10-script regression suite plus retry/DLQ re-run clean.
